facts.fact: Statista projects US digital ad spend in the travel and leisure industry will reach $4.54 billion USD in 2023, a 12% increase from 2022 (figures as cited by StackAdapt from Statista).
facts.quote: In 2023, it’s projected that spend will reach $4.54 billion USD, a 12% increase from 2022.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that Americans go on over 2.29 billion domestic trips every year.
facts.quote: Americans go on over 2.29 billion domestic trips every year!

facts.fact: In one study cited by StackAdapt, 80% of respondents described their most recent local travel experience as positive or very positive.
facts.quote: 80% of those respondents described their most recent local travel experience as positive or very positive.

facts.fact: StackAdapt reports that 69% of consumers said they are more mindful of choosing hotels and airlines that align with their values and support diversity and inclusion.
facts.quote: Sixty-nine percent of consumers said they are more mindful of choosing hotels and airlines that align with their values

facts.fact: According to American Express, 68% of travellers support airline brands that are sustainable and 55% support airline brands that are carbon negative.
facts.quote: many are looking to support airline brands that are sustainable (68%) and carbon negative (55%).

facts.fact: StackAdapt states it is partnered with Adara to offer solutions for travel campaigns, including unique audiences, insights and targeting.
facts.quote: StackAdapt is partnered with Adara, the leader in travel data, to offer solutions for travel campaigns, including unique audiences, insights and targeting.

facts.fact: StackAdapt says a brand lift study can show how likely travellers are to pay more for access to a hotel perk, as well as the consumer's perception of a chain after seeing an ad that mentions it.
facts.quote: The study can discover how likely travellers are to pay more for access to the hotel perk, as well as the perception a consumer has about the chain after seeing an ad that mentions it.
